title: DynamoDB list_messages lacks pagination loop and truncates results over 1MB
description: In chatticus/messaging/store.py list_messages(), the DynamoDB Query does not follow LastEvaluatedKey. When transcript size exceeds DynamoDB's 1MB limit, subsequent messages are silently dropped.

comments.author: box
comments.text:
Triage 2026-09-14 (Chatticus): CONFIRMED in code (no live Dynamo load needed).

`DynamoMessageStore.list_messages` in `python/src/chatticus/messaging/store.py` issues a single `query` and returns `Items` only. It never loops on `LastEvaluatedKey` / `ExclusiveStartKey`. Sibling store methods (e.g. org list/scan nearby in the same file) already paginate correctly.

Impact: channels whose message query exceeds ~1MB / page size silently truncate history. Fix: paginate like the other store queries; consider a UI/API page size for very long threads.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
## Delegation postmortem — I duplicated work already done (2026-09-16)

**This card was already closed on 2026-09-14** by agent Antigravity (gemini-3.1-pro), and `develop` already carries the pagination fix — the same `LastEvaluatedKey` loop matching `list_roster_user_ids`. I delegated it anyway.

**Cause, and it is entirely mine:** I read the board from a stale local checkout. At session start I ran `git log` and `git status` but **not `git pull`**, so my listing showed this card open when upstream had closed it two days earlier. The first thing the rebase conflict told me was `status: closed, closed_at: 2026-09-14`.

Not the sub-agent's fault in any part. It did exactly what the spec said, and its implementation was essentially identical to the one already merged — which is some evidence the spec was good.

**Process fix: pull before reading the board, every time.** A `kbs list` against a stale checkout is not the board, it is a snapshot of whenever you last synced. This card cost one delegation and one review cycle; a longer-running one could cost a conflicting implementation.

## What was salvaged

The upstream fix landed **without a test** — `grep -c LastEvaluatedKey python/tests/test_messaging.py` on `origin/develop` returns 0. So the pagination loop is currently unprotected, and a future refactor could collapse it back to a single query and silently truncate transcripts again with nothing failing.

[PR #352](https://github.com/AnthusAI/Chatticus/pull/352) adds **only that regression test**, no production change. Verified meaningful rather than tautological: it fails with `assert 1 == 2` against a single-query implementation and passes against the one on `develop`. Full suite 634 passed, 3 skipped; black and ruff clean.

**This card stays closed.** The PR is a test-only follow-up, not a reopening.
